transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

Lately I keep jumping into big plans and trips without thinking, and it’s starting to cause problems for my family. My wife and kids got really worried after I took a long drive recently without telling anyone, so they insisted I come in to get checked out.
Can you tell me more about what happens before you jump into these big plans, do you feel an overwhelming urge or excitement that you can't control?

Yes, absolutely—I wake up after just a few hours of sleep feeling on top of the world and buzzing with an intense energy that has me pacing the floors. I get this physical pressure in my chest that drives me to start planning and organizing immediately, and it feels impossible to slow down or think about the consequences until afterward.
Do you also experience periods where your mood shifts to feeling extremely low, sad, or hopeless, or is it mostly this high-energy, excited state that you've been describing?

No, I haven't felt low or sad at all; it's been almost entirely this buzzing, high-energy state where I feel on top of the world. However, I do get highly wound up and swing into feeling very irritable and frustrated when people try to slow me down or question my plans.
Can you estimate how long these high-energy episodes typically last, and do you experience a return to a normal mood in between these episodes?

This high-energy state has been going on continuously for about a month now, starting right around the time my supervisor pushed me to set a firm retirement date. Before this past month, I was always my usual warm, steady self, so this is actually the very first time I've ever experienced anything like this.

You mentioned this high-energy state started around the time your supervisor pushed you to set a firm retirement date, but you've had it continuously for a month; can you think of any other significant life events or stressors that might have contributed to this change, or was it really just this one event that seems to have triggered it?

Yes, around that same time, several of my younger relatives moved away for work. I felt this sudden, strong pressure to make up for their absence, which drove me to start frantically organizing more church events, youth mentoring, and family gatherings to fill the gap.

You've mentioned that this high-energy state has been continuous for about a month, but can you recall if there have been any brief periods, even just a day or two, where you felt your normal self again before the high energy resumed?

No, there haven't been any breaks or normal days at all. It has been completely non-stop, 24/7 high energy and planning since my supervisor pushed for that retirement date. I haven't had a single day this past month where I felt like my usual, steady self.
Have you noticed any changes in your spending habits or engaging in impulsive buying sprees during this high-energy period?

Yes, I’ve been volunteering the little savings my wife and I have to fund these big events and projects I suddenly dream up. I've also promised to host huge gatherings and fix up people's houses, even though our bank account really can't handle it. It's only afterward that I realize how risky and unfair all of this is to my wife.
Have you ever experienced any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted less than a month, or has this been a single, continuous episode since it started?

No, I've never had anything like this happen before in my life. This has been one single, continuous episode that started about a month ago, right after my supervisor pushed me to set a firm retirement date.
During these episodes of high energy, have you experienced any thoughts or beliefs that seem unreal or detached from reality, such as hearing voices or feeling like you have special powers?

No, I haven't heard any voices or believed that I have special powers. While I sometimes feel on top of the world, like I'm the only one who really knows what needs to be done around here, I haven't felt detached from reality in that way.

You mentioned this high-energy state has been continuous for about a month, but to clarify, have you had any periods where the intensity of this energy and these plans decreased slightly, even if the overall state remained elevated?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed any clear drops in my energy, as this past month has just felt like one continuous, non-stop blur.

You mentioned feeling like you're on top of the world and that you're the only one who really knows what needs to be done, can you tell me more about what you mean by that, do you feel like you have an increased sense of self-importance or grandeur?

Yes, I've had this intense rush of confidence, feeling like I have the perfect vision for our church projects and that I'm the only one who can get them done right. Because of that, I get highly frustrated and snap at my wife or the pastor over the smallest pushback, even though I later regret being so irritable.
Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like your ideas or plans were so superior that you became frustrated or angry with others for not immediately agreeing with you?

Yes, recently when I tried to push some new church projects, my pastor and my wife suggested we slow down, and I snapped at them because I felt like I was the only one who knew what really needed to be done. I got highly frustrated over that tiny bit of pushback and found it incredibly hard to dial it down, even though I could see I was upsetting them. It's just very hard to stop when I'm so convinced my plans are right.
Have you experienced any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning, or required hospitalization, due to your high-energy episodes and impulsive behaviors?

I haven't been hospitalized, but this has severely strained my commitments and my relationships. I've missed several mentoring sessions, upset church leaders by barging in with half-baked plans, and my wife says she can no longer rely on me or feel safe after I disappeared on those sudden solo drives.

You've described a continuous month of high energy without a break, but can you recall if there were any brief moments, perhaps just a few hours, where your energy levels or mood seemed to shift or normalize before returning to this high state?
I don't really recall any moments where my energy normalized or went back to my usual self. It has just felt like a continuous, non-stop blur of high energy for the entire past month.

Can you confirm again if you've had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt a noticeable decrease in your energy levels or a return to a more normal mood, or has it been a completely consistent high-energy state for the entire month?

Yes, it has been completely consistent for the entire month without any breaks or returns to normal. I feel constantly buzzing with energy day and night, and even when my mood swings, it only goes between feeling on top of the world and feeling highly irritable, never returning to a calm state.

You've mentioned this high-energy state has been continuous for about a month, but to further clarify, are you certain there haven't been any periods, even as short as a few days, where you felt a slight decrease in energy or a moment of normalcy before the high energy resumed, which could help differentiate between a manic episode and a hypomanic episode?

I am absolutely certain there haven't been any breaks or normal days since my supervisor pushed me to set that retirement date. It has been a completely continuous, non-stop buzz of high energy for the entire month. I haven't had even a day or two of feeling like my usual, calm self.
